claims.text: Alloying can introduce a controlled amount of lattice distortion into high-entropy alloys.
Introducing lattice distortion through alloying can improve elevated-temperature mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys.
The intervention applies to as-cast or annealed high-entropy alloys.
Lattice distortion enhances diffusion at elevated temperatures.
Lattice distortion enhances precipitation of strengthening phases.
Enhanced precipitation of strengthening phases increases resistance to deformation at elevated temperatures.
Enhanced precipitation of strengthening phases increases creep resistance at elevated temperatures.
The intervention will improve yield strength by at least 20% relative to an as-cast or annealed high-entropy alloy without the introduced lattice distortion.
The intervention will improve creep resistance by at least 20% relative to an as-cast or annealed high-entropy alloy without the introduced lattice distortion.
The predicted effect should hold between 500°C and 800°C.
The proposed intervention is applicable to gas-turbine and aerospace components.
An improvement of less than 10% in both yield strength and creep resistance would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts at least a 20% improvement, but the experiment only falsifies it below 10%. Outcomes from 10% to under 20% would fail the stated prediction without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
The conditions specify temperatures above 500°C, whereas the boundary includes 500°C itself.
